subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw keep heartbeats serialized on the existing runner with mitigations, or sponsor a separate heartbeat execution lane with explicit session, delivery, retry, and tool-side-effect boundaries?
rationale: The code path is intentionally serialized/backpressured today, and changing it affects core session state and message delivery semantics rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design Isolated Heartbeat Execution
options.body: Define a first-class heartbeat isolation contract, then implement a separate lane only after session state, delivery ordering, retries, and tool side effects are specified.

options.title: Keep Serialized Heartbeats
options.body: Keep the current runner model and rely on mitigations such as isolated sessions, light context, model overrides, skip behavior, and the narrower retry-cadence fix.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Keep this issue as a design tracker and handle concrete regressions through narrower issues such as the requests-in-flight retry bug.

recommendation.title: Design Isolated Heartbeat Execution
recommendation.body: Define a first-class heartbeat isolation contract, then implement a separate lane only after session state, delivery ordering, retries, and tool side effects are specified.

likelyOwner.reason: The unified heartbeat runner and drift-fix history make this the best available routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
